# Notebook magics


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

BPL adds `%bpl` and `%%bpl` magics to IPython. Both magics evaluate code
in `basedpl.bpl`, the workspace also used by Python calls through `bpl`.

`%bpl` returns a `basedpl.Array` or a `basedpl.Function`. `%%bpl`
displays what the BPL prompt would show, including implicit expression
results. Registering the magics gives `basedpl.bpl` the BPL prompt’s
display settings: matrices, nested arrays and strings are shown in
boxes, and functions as trees. The notebook’s rich display of Python
values uses the same settings, because it reads the same workspace.

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
from basedpl import Array, bpl
from IPython.utils.capture import capture_output
import numpy as np
```

## Rendering output

[`AplOut._repr_html_`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/magics.html#aplout._repr_html_)
HTML-escapes the text and wraps it in `<pre class="bpl_out">`, which
preserves BPL spacing.

``` python
out = AplOut('1 < 2')
assert '&lt;' in out._repr_html_()
out
```

<pre class="bpl_out">1 &lt; 2</pre>

## The magics

Each call to `%bpl` or `%%bpl` displays a JavaScript snippet that calls
the page’s `loadBplInput` function when the page has one, and otherwise
imports the BPL input method from a CDN. The browser keeps one symbol
bar, including when a Solveit dialog is reopened on the same kernel.

`%bpl` displays any explicit output as BPL produces it, and returns the
expression’s native value. Ending a `%%bpl` cell with `;` suppresses all
of its display while still evaluating the cell. Output produced before
an error is displayed before the error is raised.

Press Tab to complete user and system names in `%bpl` and `%%bpl`. Tab
completion reads the workspace without evaluating anything.

`%%bpl` displays the result of each expression. Assignments are
[shy](terms.qmd#term-shy) and display nothing.

``` python
%%bpl
m←2 3ρι6
m×10
```

    <IPython.core.display.Javascript object>

<pre class="bpl_out">┌→───────┐
↓ 0 10 20│
│30 40 50│
└~───────┘</pre>

`%bpl` returns a `basedpl.Array`. Use `.np` to convert it to a NumPy
array or `.py` to convert it to a Python value. BPL parses comments
itself. A [`⍝`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/lamp.html)
inside a quoted string doesn’t start a comment.

``` python
z = %bpl m ⍝ a matrix
test_is(type(z), Array)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(z.np, [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]])
test_eq(magic.bpl('"a⍝b" ⍝ comment').py, 'a⍝b')
z
```

    <IPython.core.display.Javascript object>

    <IPython.core.display.Javascript object>

    ┌→────┐
    ↓0 1 2│
    │3 4 5│
    └~────┘

Python values bound through `bpl` are visible to the magics. Integers
from Python stay exact integers in BPL, and the result converts back to
a Python `int`.

``` python
bpl(x=np.arange(1, 4))
value = %bpl +/x
test_eq(value.py, 6)
test_is(type(value.py), int)
value
```

    <IPython.core.display.Javascript object>

    6ₓ₈

BPL’s display commands also work in `%%bpl`.

``` python
%%bpl
]Display [[1 2] "ab"]
```

    <IPython.core.display.Javascript object>

<pre class="bpl_out">┌→───────────┐
│ ┌→──┐ &quot;ab&quot; │
│ │1 2│      │
│ └~──┘      │
└∊───────────┘</pre>

A `%%bpl` cell ending in `;` still updates the workspace.

``` python
%%bpl
quiet←7;
```

    <IPython.core.display.Javascript object>

SVG elements and custom MIME renderers are displayed in `%%bpl` cells
and when returned as Python values.

``` python
%%bpl
circle←•element "circle"
•svg circle ["cx":50 "cy":50 "r":30 "fill":"orange"]
```

## Names and help

Use `]help name` for help and `]help name -source` for source, in either
magic. Leading comments in a dfn supply its help text. `]help` inspects
a function without calling it.

``` python
%%bpl
double←{⍝ Double the argument
⎕←"called" ◇ ω×2}
```

    <IPython.core.display.Javascript object>

``` python
with capture_output() as cap: magic.bpl(']help double')
assert 'Double the argument' in cap.outputs[-1].data['text/markdown']
with capture_output() as cap: magic.bpl('', ']help double -source')
assert '⎕←"called"' in cap.outputs[-1].data['text/markdown']
test_eq(len(cap.outputs), 2)
```

Because tab completion reads the `basedpl.bpl` workspace, it includes
names defined after the magics were registered. Tab does not complete
BPL names inside quoted text or comments.

``` python
from IPython.core.completer import provisionalcompleter
```

``` python
shell = get_ipython()
for text, expected in [('%bpl dou', 'double'), ('v = %bpl dou', 'double'), ('%%bpl\n1+•sr', '•src'), ("%%bpl\n''' dou", 'double')]:
    with provisionalcompleter(): matches = list(shell.Completer.completions(text, len(text)))
    assert expected in [m.text for m in matches]
for text in ['%%bpl\n"dou', '%%bpl\n⍝ dou', 'ordinary_python']:
    with provisionalcompleter(): matches = list(shell.Completer.completions(text, len(text)))
    assert not any(m.type == 'BPL name' for m in matches)
```

## Errors and workspace state

An error reports its source location, and assignments completed before
the error remain in the workspace. Incomplete input raises a syntax
error and leaves the workspace unchanged.

``` python
with capture_output() as cap: test_fail(lambda: magic.bpl('', '⎕←42 ◇ 1÷"a"'), contains='DOMAIN ERROR')
assert '42' in cap.outputs[-1].data['text/html']
test_fail(lambda: magic.bpl('', '{ω+1'), contains='SYNTAX ERROR')
test_eq(magic.bpl('quiet').py, 9)
```

    <IPython.core.display.Javascript object>

    <IPython.core.display.Javascript object>

Set `bpl.timeout` to the time limit in seconds for each evaluation.
Press Ctrl-C to interrupt the evaluation. Output produced before an
evaluation is cancelled is still displayed. The workspace keeps its
names after cancellation. Native-library calls and individual BigInt
operations can delay cancellation.

## Installation

`%load_ext basedpl.notebooks` registers the magics in the current
kernel. `bpl-install-magic` adds `basedpl.notebooks` to the default
IPython profile, so that IPython loads it at startup. Registering the
magics does not start a `bpl --worker` subprocess.

## Symbol input

`%bpl` and `%%bpl` load BPL’s browser input method for typing glyphs.
[Using BPL notebooks](notebooks.ipynb#python-magics) explains the input
method.
